questions.q: What is the rule to check if a number is divisible by 5?
questions.a: A number is divisible by 5 if its last digit is either 0 or 5. A wrong answer here suggests the student is confusing this with the rule for 2, where they might incorrectly think any even number is divisible by 5.

questions.q: If you add the digits of 471 and get 12, is 471 divisible by 3? Why?
questions.a: Yes, 471 is divisible by 3 because the sum of its digits (12) is divisible by 3. If a student says "no," they likely forgot the rule for 3 or are incorrectly looking at the last digit instead of the sum.

questions.q: Is the number 894 divisible by 2? Show your steps.
questions.a: Yes, because the last digit is 4, which is an even number. If a student answers "no," they might be trying to divide the whole number instead of checking only the last digit.

questions.q: Compare the rules for 2 and 5. What do they have in common?
questions.a: Both rules depend only on the last digit of the number. If a student tries to bring in the rule for 3, they are confusing the "last digit" method with the "sum of digits" method.

questions.q: Can a number be divisible by both 2 and 5? If so, what must its last digit be?
questions.a: Yes, the last digit must be 0. If a student says "5," they forgot that 5 is not even, so it cannot be divisible by 2.

questions.q: Create a 3-digit number that is divisible by 3 but not by 2 or 5. Explain how you chose it.
questions.a: A possible answer is 333 (sum is 9, so divisible by 3; last digit is odd, so not divisible by 2 or 5). A poor answer would show a number that is even or ends in 5, failing the "not by 2 or 5" condition.
